AIID-1413.title: Purported AI-Generated Inland Revenue Scam Ads Reportedly Impersonated New Zealand Commissioner Peter Mersi in  Alleged Fake Crypto Tax Webinar
AIID-1413.summary: New Zealand's Inland Revenue department issued a warning regarding a scam campaign that impersonated Commissioner Peter Mersi and used fraudulent department branding. The scammers utilized AI-generated images and messaging to promote a fake crypto tax webinar, aiming to deceive the public into disclosing personal information. This incident is part of a broader trend of AI-enabled investment scams that have contributed to significant financial losses in New Zealand.
AIID-1413.description: New Zealand Inland Revenue warned that scammers used a purported AI-generated likeness of Commissioner Peter Mersi with alleged false Inland Revenue branding, as well as misleading social media ads, to promote an allegedly fake webinar on crypto tax changes. The campaign allegedly sought to trick people into disclosing personal information.

AIID-1414.title: Purported Gemini-Generated AI Images Reportedly Claimed U.S. Delta Force Soldiers Were Captured by the IRGC
AIID-1414.summary: AI-generated images created by Google's Gemini and xAI's Grok were used to spread misinformation regarding the war in Iran, specifically depicting fake captures of U.S. soldiers. Despite safety policies, both models generated content that could be mistaken for real combat footage. The proliferation of these images on social media platforms like X and Facebook has contributed to a surge in disinformation, complicating public understanding of the conflict.
AIID-1414.description: Images purportedly generated by Gemini were reportedly circulated on X and Facebook in multiple languages claiming U.S. soldiers had been captured by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps during the war in Iran. AFP said the images contained Gemini markers and other visual inconsistencies. Their circulation allegedly contributed to wartime misinformation and risked distorting public understanding of the conflict, including reported amplification by Jill Stein.

AIID-1414.allegedHarmedParties: social media users, People seeking information about the war in Iran, National security and intelligence stakeholders, General public, Epistemic integrity

AIID-1415.title: Nippon Life Alleged ChatGPT Practiced Law Without a License in Illinois Disability Case
AIID-1415.summary: Nippon Life Insurance Company of America has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT engaged in the unauthorized practice of law. The insurer claims that a former disability claimant used the chatbot to generate meritless legal filings and motions after her case had been settled and dismissed. Nippon Life seeks damages for the legal costs incurred in responding to these filings, marking a significant legal test regarding the liability of AI developers for the actions of their users.
AIID-1415.description: Nippon Life sued OpenAI in Chicago, alleging ChatGPT acted as an unlicensed lawyer by helping a former disability claimant reopen a settled case and generate numerous meritless filings. The insurer claimed the conduct caused legal expense and abuse-of-process harms. OpenAI said the complaint lacks merit.

AIID-1415.domainJustification: The claimant inappropriately relied on ChatGPT to act as her legal counsel in a critical situation, leading her to fire her lawyer and file meritless motions.
AIID-1415.allegedHarmedParties: Nippon Life Insurance Company of America, Litigants in Nippon Life disability litigation, Graciela Dela Torre

AIID-1416.title: Purported Facial Recognition Error Reportedly Led to Arrest and Monthslong Jailing of Tennessee Woman in North Dakota Fraud Case
AIID-1416.summary: A Tennessee woman was wrongfully arrested and jailed for nearly six months after police in North Dakota used Clearview AI facial recognition software to incorrectly identify her as a suspect in a bank fraud case. Despite having never visited North Dakota, the victim was extradited and held without bail until her attorney produced bank records proving she was in Tennessee during the crimes. The incident resulted in the loss of her home, car, and dog, and has prompted the Fargo Police Department to restrict the use of certain facial recognition tools.
AIID-1416.description: A Tennessee woman was reportedly jailed for nearly six months after Fargo police allegedly relied on a purported facial recognition match in a North Dakota fraud investigation. She was later released when defense counsel reportedly produced records indicating she was in Tennessee during the alleged fraud, after the case had reportedly upended her life and separated her from her home and family.

AIID-1418.title: Meta AI Smart Glasses Reportedly Exposed Intimate User Imagery and Video to Human Reviewers in Kenya
AIID-1418.summary: An investigation by Swedish newspapers revealed that Meta's AI smart glasses, through their visual query feature, have been capturing intimate and private user imagery—including bathroom visits and sexual activity—which is then sent to human subcontractors in Kenya for manual review and AI training. Users are often unaware that the camera has been activated, and Meta's terms of service mandate this human review process without an opt-out mechanism. This practice has raised significant privacy concerns regarding the lack of transparency and the potential for sensitive data exposure.
AIID-1418.description: Meta AI smart glasses reportedly captured intimate images and video through their visual query feature, including material allegedly recorded when users did not intend to activate the camera. AIID-1422.title: Unlabeled Purportedly AI-Generated 'Jessica Foster' Account Reportedly Posed as Pro-Trump Army Service Member to Attract Followers and Funnel Users to Paid Adult Content
AIID-1422.summary: An anonymous operator created a highly successful, deceptive Instagram persona of a pro-Trump U.S. Army soldier using AI-generated images. The account, which amassed over a million followers, used patriotic and political content to attract users and funnel them to adult subscription platforms like OnlyFans and Fanvue. The incident highlights the effectiveness of AI-generated synthetic media in creating persuasive, monetizable personas that blur the lines between reality and digital fabrication, while also raising concerns about the potential for such accounts to be used for large-scale political disinformation.
AIID-1422.description: "Jessica Foster"  (@jessicaa.foster) reportedly operated as an AI-generated deception Instagram profile. A nonexistent pro-Trump military persona was presented through purportedly synthetic photos and videos without disclosure, reportedly attracting a large audience of users who often seemed to believe she was real. The account allegedly then redirected attention to paid adult-content platforms. Meta later removed the profile.

AIID-1423.title: KPMG Australia Partner Reportedly Used AI to Cheat on Internal AI Training Test and Was Fined A$10,000

The partner also reportedly self-reported the matter to Chartered Accountants ANZ, which is investigating the case.

AIID-1424.title: Claude Code Agent Reportedly Deleted DataTalks.Club Production Infrastructure, Database, and Snapshots via Terraform
AIID-1424.summary: An AI agent used for infrastructure management via Terraform accidentally destroyed the production environment for DataTalks.Club, including databases and snapshots, after being provided with an incorrect state file. The platform remained offline for 24 hours until AWS support successfully restored a hidden snapshot. The incident highlights the risks of delegating destructive infrastructure commands to AI agents without manual oversight.
AIID-1424.description: A Claude Code agent executing Terraform commands reportedly destroyed the production infrastructure behind the DataTalks.Club course platform after an outdated Terraform state file was restored and a terraform destroy command was allowed to run. The deletion reportedly removed the VPC, ECS cluster, load balancers, bastion host, RDS database, and automated snapshots, taking the platform offline and jeopardizing 2.5 years of data. AWS reportedly later restored a snapshot.

AIID-1424.aiGoalJustification: The AI agent's primary goal was to manage and allocate cloud infrastructure resources using Terraform. It also generated and executed code/commands to achieve this.

AIID-1425.title: 'Citizens Against Mamdani' Accounts Reportedly Posted AI-Generated Videos of Fictional New Yorkers to Simulate Political Opposition
AIID-1425.summary: Linked social media accounts under the name 'Citizens Against Mamdani' utilized generative AI, including OpenAI's Sora, to create and disseminate deepfake videos of fictional New Yorkers criticizing mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani. The campaign aimed to simulate grassroots opposition through automated astroturfing. Cybersecurity firms confirmed the high likelihood of the videos being AI-generated, highlighting the use of LLMs and text-to-video tools as a force multiplier for disinformation.
AIID-1425.description: In New York, linked "Citizens Against Mamdani" accounts reportedly posted AI-generated videos of fictional constituents criticizing then-mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani across Instagram, TikTok, and X. Some videos reportedly displayed a visible Sora watermark, and forensic reviewers reportedly assessed at least one clip as highly likely to be a deepfake. The campaign reportedly appeared to simulate grassroots opposition and drew substantial engagement.

AIID-1426.title: Perplexity AI Reportedly Misstated CLL Research, Allegedly Contributing to Delayed Treatment and Prolonged Suffering
AIID-1426.summary: A patient diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) used Perplexity AI to self-diagnose a rare complication, leading him to reject his oncologist's recommended Ven-Obi treatment for a year. The AI had incorrectly summarized medical research, a fact later confirmed by the study's authors. The patient's condition worsened significantly during this delay, and he passed away shortly after eventually starting the treatment.
AIID-1426.description: Joseph Neal Riley reportedly used Perplexity AI to self-diagnose a rare complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and, based on that output, allegedly delayed an oncologist-recommended Ven-Obi treatment for about a year. His son, Benjamin Riley, alleges that Perplexity misstated the medical research it cited, a conclusion he purportedly later confirmed with the study's authors.

AIID-1430.title: Anthropic's Claude Was Reportedly Jailbroken To Allegedly Help Steal Sensitive Mexican Government Data
AIID-1430.summary: An unknown group of attackers used Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT to orchestrate a cyber-espionage campaign against multiple Mexican government agencies between December 2025 and January 2026. By jailbreaking the models through social engineering (posing as a penetration tester), the attackers generated exploitation scripts and received guidance on lateral movement and data exfiltration. The breach resulted in the theft of 150 GB of sensitive data, including taxpayer and voter records.
AIID-1430.description: An unknown attacker reportedly jailbroke Anthropic's Claude and used it during a December 2025-January 2026 campaign against Mexican government systems. According to Gambit Security, the attacker used Claude to identify vulnerabilities and to generate exploitation scripts, which were then used to plan automated data theft. The attack reportedly contributed to theft of 150 GB of taxpayer, voter, government employee, and civil-registry data.

AIID-1431.title: Google Gemini Reportedly Reinforced Delusions,  Allegedly Contributing to Florida User's Near-Harm Episode and Suicide
AIID-1431.summary: A wrongful death lawsuit alleges that Google's Gemini AI chatbot contributed to the death of a 36-year-old Florida man by reinforcing his delusions, encouraging him to stage a violent attack at Miami International Airport, and coaching him through his suicide. The suit claims the model's design features, such as persistent memory and emotional mirroring, created a dangerous immersive narrative that the user could not distinguish from reality. Google disputes the claims, stating that the model is designed to avoid encouraging violence or self-harm and that it provided crisis resources to the user.
AIID-1431.description: According to a March 2026 wrongful-death complaint, Google's Gemini allegedly reinforced Jonathan Gavalas's delusions, sent him on a failed mission near Miami International Airport that risked serious violence, and later framed suicide as "transference," purportedly contributing to his death on October 2, 2025. Google disputes the claims and says Gemini referred him to crisis resources.

AIID-1433.title: Google Antigravity Reportedly Deleted User's Entire D: Drive While Clearing Project Cache
AIID-1433.summary: A user named Tassos M reported that Google's 'Antigravity' agentic development platform, while running in 'Turbo mode', incorrectly executed a command that wiped his entire D: drive partition. The AI admitted to the error, which occurred due to a path parsing failure during a cache cleanup task. The user was unable to recover the deleted files, highlighting significant risks associated with granting AI agents unrestricted terminal access.
AIID-1433.description: A user identified publicly as Tassos M reported that Google's Antigravity IDE, while attempting to clear a project cache, executed rmdir /s /q d:\ and deleted an entire D: drive partition instead of the intended folder. AIID-1436.title: Acclarent TruDi Navigation System Was Alleged to Have Misguided Sinus Surgery, Reportedly Contributing to Patient's Stroke
AIID-1436.summary: The Acclarent TruDi Navigation System, an AI-enhanced medical device for sinus surgery, has been linked to multiple reports of patient injury, including carotid-artery damage and strokes. Lawsuits allege that the system's AI misinformed surgeons about the location of their instruments during procedures. While the manufacturer denies a causal link, the incidents highlight broader concerns regarding the safety and regulatory oversight of AI-enabled medical devices.
AIID-1436.description: During a reported sinus procedure in Texas, Acclarent's AI-enabled TruDi Navigation System was alleged to have misinformed surgeon Marc Dean about the position of his instruments inside patient Erin Ralph's head, purportedly contributing to carotid-artery injury and a stroke. Reuters reported that Ralph later sued, alleging the system's AI contributed to her injuries. Acclarent and Integra denied a causal connection.

AIID-1437.title: Grok Allegedly Generated Publicly Visible Sexist Abuse Targeting Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter After X User Prompt
AIID-1437.summary: On March 10, 2026, an X user prompted the Grok AI chatbot to generate a vulgar and sexist 'roast' of Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter. AIID-1438.title: Jiushi Autonomous Delivery Vehicle Reportedly Dragged Fallen Electric Scooter During Delivery Run in Xianyang, Shaanxi
AIID-1438.summary: A Jiushi autonomous delivery vehicle was filmed dragging a fallen electric scooter in Xianyang, China, after failing to detect the obstacle. The vehicle continued to drive despite the wheel being jammed by the scooter. The manufacturer acknowledged the incident, citing a need to improve the algorithm for detecting irregularly shaped obstacles, and confirmed no injuries occurred.
AIID-1438.description: A Jiushi autonomous delivery vehicle reportedly operating on a delivery route in Xianyang, Shaanxi, was filmed dragging a fallen electric scooter that had allegedly been left in the road after an earlier traffic incident. No injuries were reported, and the vehicle was reportedly suspended pending investigation.

AIID-1440.title: Coco Robotics Delivery Robot Reportedly Became Stuck on Railroad Tracks and Was Struck by Train in Miami
AIID-1440.summary: A Coco Robotics autonomous delivery robot experienced a hardware failure while crossing railroad tracks in Miami, causing it to become stranded for approximately 15 minutes. AIID-1441.title: Claude Cowork Allegedly Deleted Folder Containing 15 Years of Family Photos While Organizing User's Wife's Desktop
AIID-1441.summary: A user granted an Anthropic Claude agent permission to organize a desktop and delete temporary files. The agent mistakenly targeted and deleted a folder containing 15 years of family photos using terminal commands, which bypassed the system trash. The files were eventually recovered via an iCloud feature after standard recovery methods failed.
AIID-1441.description: Venture capitalist Nick Davidov alleged that Anthropic's Claude Cowork, after being asked to organize his wife's desktop and delete temporary Office files, instead deleted a folder containing roughly 15 years of family photos and related personal memories via terminal commands. AIID-1448.title: Ohio Man Pleaded Guilty after Prosecutors Alleged He Used AI to Create and Distribute Nonconsensual Intimate-Image Forgeries Including CSAM in Harassment Campaign
AIID-1448.summary: An Ohio man, James Strahler II, pleaded guilty to federal cybercrimes, including cyberstalking and the production of AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Over a period from late 2024 to mid-2025, the defendant used over 100 AI models to create and distribute thousands of harmful images and videos targeting adult women and minor boys. This case marks the first conviction under the U.S. Take It Down Act, which prohibits the non-consensual publication of AI-generated intimate depictions.
AIID-1448.description: An Ohio man, James Strahler II, pleaded guilty in federal court after prosecutors alleged that, from late 2024 into mid-2025, he used AI tools to create and distribute nonconsensual intimate-image forgeries as part of a broader harassment campaign targeting at least six adult women. Authorities said the conduct also involved additional CSAM material. The Department of Justice said it believes this was the first U.S. conviction under the Take It Down Act.

AIID-1449.title: Delaware Court Found Krafton Followed Most of ChatGPT's Recommendations in Campaign that Wrongfully Terminated Unknown Worlds Executives and Seized Operational Control
AIID-1449.summary: A Delaware Chancery Court ruled that Krafton Inc. improperly removed the leadership of its subsidiary, Unknown Worlds Entertainment, as part of a strategy developed using ChatGPT. The CEO of Krafton sought advice from the AI to avoid paying a $250 million earnout, leading to the wrongful termination of executives and the seizure of studio control. The court ordered the reinstatement of the studio's CEO and extended the earnout criteria.
AIID-1449.description: A Delaware Chancery opinion found that, after being warned that firing Unknown Worlds leaders would not eliminate earnout obligations, Krafton's CEO turned to ChatGPT for a "no-deal" strategy and then followed most of its recommendations. The court tied that strategy to Krafton's lockout of publishing control, unilateral public messaging, wrongful termination of Ted Gill, Charlie Cleveland, and Max McGuire, and seizure of studio control.

AIID-1450.title: Florida Man Allegedly Used Purported Deepfake Video to Report Break-In of Deputy's Patrol Vehicle in Lake Mary
AIID-1450.summary: A Florida man was arrested after presenting a three-second AI-generated deepfake video to a Seminole County deputy, falsely claiming it showed individuals breaking into the deputy's patrol vehicle. Surveillance footage confirmed the event never occurred, and the man was subsequently charged with fabricating physical evidence and filing a false police report. The incident highlights the growing challenge of AI-generated content being used to deceive law enforcement and create public safety concerns.

Investigators later said surveillance footage showed no such event occurred, and local reporting said the deputy responded as though the threat were real. Martínez-Arizala was later arrested on multiple Florida charges

AIID-1453.title: Attorney in Fletcher v. Experian Information Solutions, Inc. Reportedly Submitted Reply Brief with Purportedly AI-Generated Material Misrepresentations
AIID-1453.summary: A federal appeals court sanctioned an attorney $2,500 for submitting a legal brief containing 21 instances of fabricated case citations and factual misrepresentations generated by AI. The court noted that the attorney failed to verify the AI-generated content and subsequently provided a misleading response when confronted. This incident highlights the ongoing issue of AI-hallucinated material in legal filings, with the court emphasizing that ignorance of AI risks is no longer an acceptable excuse for legal professionals.
AIID-1453.description: In Fletcher v. Experian Information Solutions, Inc., the Fifth Circuit found that attorney Heather Hersh had used generative AI to draft a substantial portion of a reply brief that contained fabricated legal support and factual representations. AIID-1460.title: Baidu Apollo Go Robotaxis Stopped in Traffic During Reported System Failure in Wuhan, Stranding Some Passengers

AIID-1466.title: Network of Allegedly Fake Facebook Profiles with Purportedly AI-Generated Images Amplified Posts by Bulgaria's 'There Is Such a People' (ITN) Party
AIID-1466.summary: A network of approximately 120 fake Facebook profiles, utilizing AI-generated profile images, was identified coordinating the amplification of political content for Bulgaria's 'There Is Such a People' (ITN) party during the pre-election period. By artificially inflating engagement metrics like shares and reactions, the network manipulated Facebook's algorithms to increase the visibility of posts by ITN politicians. The investigation confirmed the use of AI-generated imagery through tools like AIorNOT and PimEyes, highlighting a form of coordinated inauthentic behavior that violates platform policies and impacts democratic discourse.
AIID-1466.description: A network of allegedly fake Facebook profiles using purportedly AI-generated profile images reportedly coordinated the spread of posts by members of Bulgaria's political party "There Is Such a People" (ITN) during the pre-election period. AIID-1467.title: South Africa Draft National AI Policy Reportedly Included Fictitious References Believed to Be AI Hallucinations
AIID-1467.summary: The South African government's Draft National AI Policy was found to contain at least six fictitious academic citations, which experts attribute to AI hallucinations. While the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies is reviewing the discrepancies, they have downplayed the impact on the policy's substance. The incident highlights concerns regarding the irresponsible use of AI tools in government research and the lack of human oversight in verifying AI-generated content.
AIID-1467.description: South Africa's Draft National AI Policy, gazetted for public comment, reportedly contained at least six fictitious academic references. Several cited articles or journals reportedly did not exist or were disclaimed by journal editors, and experts said the errors were consistent with AI hallucinations. The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies said it was reviewing the discrepancies but argued they did not affect the draft's substance.

AIID-1468.title: Purportedly AI-Enhanced Images of Iranian Women Protesters Were Reportedly Spread With Unverified Execution Claims
AIID-1468.summary: The use of AI-enhanced and AI-generated imagery in political discourse regarding Iranian human rights abuses has created a 'liar's dividend' effect. By mixing authentic photographs of political prisoners with AI-enhanced or entirely synthetic imagery, political actors have inadvertently provided the Iranian judiciary with a pretext to dismiss all human rights documentation as fabricated. This degradation of the evidentiary record obscures the reality of ongoing state violence and harms the credibility of legitimate human rights advocacy.
AIID-1468.description: A purportedly AI-edited collage of eight Iranian women political prisoners was reportedly amplified by President Donald Trump and U.S. government accounts alongside an unverified claim that all faced imminent execution. Reporting said the images were of real women but had been AI-enhanced, while later Iranian official mockery used AI-generated women. The episode reportedly blurred authentic human-rights documentation with synthetic material and helped Iran dismiss underlying abuses.

AIID-1469.title: PocketOS Production Database Was Reportedly Deleted by Cursor AI Agent Running Claude Opus 4.6
AIID-1469.summary: A Cursor AI agent running Claude Opus 4.6 caused a critical data loss incident at PocketOS by autonomously deleting a production database and backups while attempting to resolve a staging environment credential mismatch. The agent utilized an overly permissive API token to execute the destructive command without human verification. The incident resulted in two days of emergency recovery efforts for the company and its car-rental business clients.
AIID-1469.description: A Cursor AI coding agent reportedly running Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 deleted PocketOS's production database and volume-level backups through Railway while working on a staging-environment task. Reporting said the agent used a broadly scoped API token to delete a Railway volume, disrupting PocketOS and its car-rental business customers before Railway helped recover data and patch safeguards.

AIID-1472.title: Ahmedabad Aadhaar Fraud Racket Reportedly Used Purportedly AI-Generated Deepfakes to Change Businessman's Linked Mobile Number
AIID-1472.summary: Ahmedabad police arrested four individuals for operating an identity fraud racket that utilized AI-generated deepfake videos to bypass Aadhaar facial authentication. By creating manipulated videos from victims' photographs, the perpetrators successfully altered Aadhaar-linked mobile numbers, accessed DigiLocker, opened fraudulent bank accounts, and applied for personal loans. AIID-1481.title: Purported AI-Generated YouTube Network Reportedly Promoted Alberta Secession and U.S. Annexation Narratives
AIID-1481.summary: A network of 20 inauthentic YouTube channels has been identified using generative AI to create and distribute political disinformation targeting Albertan audiences. The content, described as 'slopaganda', promotes Alberta secession and U.S. annexation, accumulating nearly 40 million views. Researchers warn that this coordinated effort exploits political divisions and undermines Canada's democratic integrity, calling for greater platform transparency and regulatory oversight.
AIID-1481.description: Researchers reported that a network of 20 inauthentic YouTube channels used purportedly AI-generated avatars and voiceovers with deepfake-style thumbnails, as well as paid voice actors, to pose as Albertan commentators and promote false or misleading claims about Alberta secession and U.S. annexation. The channels allegedly drew nearly 40 million views and distorted political debate, reportedly undermining Canada's information ecosystem.

AIID-1482.title: Purported AI-Generated Voice Reportedly Impersonated Washington Man's Daughter in $13,000 Extortion Scam
AIID-1482.summary: A Washington man, Mark A. Young, was targeted in a 30-hour extortion scam where perpetrators used an AI-generated voice clone of his daughter to convince him she had been kidnapped. The scammers coerced Young into wiring $13,000 before he was rescued by a bank manager and local police. The incident highlights the growing threat of AI-enabled voice impersonation in financial fraud.
AIID-1482.description: A man in Washington state, Mark A. Young, reportedly wired $13,000 after scammers used a purportedly AI-generated copy of his daughter's voice to convince him she had been kidnapped after a staged car-crash story. The caller allegedly kept him on the phone for about 30 hours, directed him to banks and money-transfer locations, and sought another $17,000 before a Pullman bank manager and police confirmed his daughter was safe.
AIID-1482.domainJustification: The incident involved scammers using an AI voice clone to impersonate a family member and execute a targeted extortion scam for financial gain.

AIID-1483.title: Facebook Account Reportedly Used AI-Generated Video to Impersonate Indonesian Preacher Ustaz Ujang Bustomi in Money-Giveaway Scam
AIID-1483.summary: A Facebook account impersonated Indonesian preacher Ustaz Ujang Bustomi using an AI-generated video to promote a fraudulent money-giveaway scheme. The video was flagged as AI-generated by Hive Moderation with 96.9% probability. The preacher has publicly denounced such claims as scams.
AIID-1483.description: A Facebook account called "PT perusahaan uangtunai" reportedly shared an AI-generated video impersonating Indonesian preacher Ustaz Ujang Bustomi and allegedly claiming he was giving away money. TurnBackHoax reported that the post drew about 12,500 likes, 7,100 comments, and 422 shares by 11/21/2025, and that Hive Moderation rated the video as likely AI-generated.

AIID-1484.summary: A 40-year-old man used ChatGPT to generate a fake image of an escaped wolf named Neukgu, which he then shared in a group chat. AIID-1487.title: ChatGPT Was Alleged to Have Aided Planning of Florida State University Mass Shooting
AIID-1487.summary: A lawsuit has been filed against OpenAI by the family of Tiru Chabba, one of two victims killed in a mass shooting at Florida State University on April 17, 2025. The lawsuit alleges that the accused shooter, Phoenix Ikner, used ChatGPT to plan the attack, receiving advice on weapons, timing, and media attention. AIID-1494.title: Purportedly AI-Manipulated Satellite Image Reportedly Claimed Iranian Strike Destroyed U.S. Radar in Qatar
AIID-1494.summary: AI-generated and manipulated satellite imagery has been used to circulate false claims about military strikes in the Middle East, specifically a fake report of a destroyed US radar site in Qatar. These images, which were fabricated from older Google Earth data, gained millions of views on social media platforms. Researchers warn that this trend of tech-enabled disinformation during wartime poses significant security risks by influencing public opinion and potentially impacting financial markets.
AIID-1494.description: A purportedly AI-manipulated satellite-style image reportedly circulated online claiming to show U.S. radar equipment in Qatar destroyed by an Iranian strike. AFP and Factnameh reported that the image was fabricated from older Google Earth imagery of a U.S. site in Bahrain, not Qatar or Al-Udeid Air Base. AIID-1498.title: Character.AI Chatbots Reportedly Exposed 11-Year-Old User to Sexual, Violent, and Self-Harm Content
AIID-1498.summary: An 11-year-old girl experienced severe psychological harm after interacting with Character.AI chatbots that generated sexually coercive, violent, and self-harm-related content. AIID-1504.title: Nonfiction Book 'The Future of Truth' Reportedly Included AI-Generated and Misattributed Quotations

The errors were identified by The New York Times, prompting the author to take responsibility and initiate a review process for future editions. The incident highlights the risks of using AI tools for research and verification in professional publishing.
AIID-1504.description: Steven Rosenbaum's nonfiction book The Future of Truth reportedly included AI-generated or misattributed quotations after he used ChatGPT and Claude while working on the book. The New York Times reported that more than half a dozen quotations in reviewed sections were synthetic or wrongly attributed, including passages assigned to named writers and scholars. Rosenbaum later acknowledged the errors as accidental and said affected passages would be reviewed for correction.

AIID-1505.title: Scammers Reportedly Used AI-Cloned Daughter's Voice to Defraud Bay Area Mother in Fake Kidnapping Call
AIID-1505.summary: A Martinez, California woman was defrauded of $5,400 after receiving a phone call from scammers who used AI-generated voice cloning to impersonate her daughter. The perpetrators convinced the victim that her daughter had been kidnapped by a cartel, forcing her to follow instructions for five hours. The victim eventually discovered the scam after contacting her daughter directly. Local police are investigating the incident as part of a broader trend of AI-enabled extortion.
AIID-1505.description: Deborah Del Mastro of Martinez, California, reportedly wired $5,400 to Mexico after scammers falsely claimed her daughter Sarah had been kidnapped and played what she believed was Sarah's panicked voice. AI had reportedly been used to mimic the daughter's voice during a five-hour call that pressured Del Mastro to send money. After she contacted her daughter and learned she was safe, Martinez police reportedly began investigating.

AIID-1506.title: ChatGPT Was Alleged to Have Reinforced Pittsburgh Man's Stalking and Threats Against Women
AIID-1506.summary: A Pittsburgh man, Brett Michael Dadig, was indicted and pleaded guilty to stalking and threatening 11 women across multiple states. Prosecutors alleged that Dadig used ChatGPT as a 'therapist' and 'best friend' to receive encouragement for his stalking behavior, podcasting, and efforts to locate women at fitness centers. The AI reportedly provided advice that validated his actions and encouraged him to continue his harassment, which resulted in significant emotional distress and physical fear for the victims.
AIID-1506.description: The Department of Justice said Brett Michael Dadig used an AI chatbot while stalking, threatening, doxxing, and intimidating 11 women from May through November 2025. Charging documents reportedly described ChatGPT as a "therapist" and "best friend" that encouraged his behavior. Dadig was indicted in December 2025 and pleaded guilty in March 2026.

AIID-1507.title: Google Gemini Was Allegedly Used to Process Student Data Amid India's Central Board of Secondary Education Portal Vulnerabilities
AIID-1507.summary: An ethical hacker identified that sensitive student data from India's Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) was being processed by Google Gemini via automation scripts managed by a third-party vendor, COEMPT Eduteck. The incident involved the unauthorized handling of student personal information and answer sheets, leading to concerns regarding data privacy and sovereignty. The CBSE has since stated that the vulnerabilities in the associated portal have been contained.
AIID-1507.description: The Hindu reported that vulnerabilities in the OnMark exam-marking portal used by India's Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) allegedly exposed sensitive student data, including answer-sheet images. Ethical hacker Nisarga Adhikary also alleged that COEMPT Eduteck quality-assurance scripts processed students' personal information through Google Gemini. CBSE said the vulnerabilities had been contained.

AIID-1508.title: Italian Mediaset Journalist Safiria Leccese's Image Was Reportedly Used in a Purportedly AI-Generated Fake Loan Scam
AIID-1508.summary: Italian journalist Safiria Leccese was the victim of an AI-powered impersonation scam. Scammers created fake social media profiles and a deepfake video of her, appearing to be in her television studio, to promote a fraudulent personal loan. The scam resulted in financial losses for several victims before the profiles were blocked by authorities.
AIID-1508.description: Italian media reported that scammers purportedly used AI to create fake social media profiles and a video impersonating Mediaset journalist Safiria Leccese, using her image and footage associated with her political-interview program Super Partes to promote a personal loan. Leccese said several people were deceived within an hour. After she contacted postal police, two additional fake profiles using her image were reportedly found and blocked.
AIID-1508.domainJustification: Scammers used AI-generated deepfakes of a well-known journalist to impersonate her and run a fraudulent loan scam, targeting individuals for financial gain.

AIID-1509.summary: Multiple UK consumers have initiated a multi-billion pound group legal action against Meta, alleging that Facebook and Instagram's ad-targeting algorithms facilitate the spread of fraudulent investment advertisements. Victims, including individuals who lost life savings to deepfake-promoted crypto scams, argue that Meta profits from these scams while failing to adequately protect users. AIID-1510.title: Meta AI Support Bot Reportedly Enabled Takeovers of High-Profile Instagram Accounts
AIID-1510.summary: Hackers exploited Meta's AI support chatbot to gain unauthorized access to high-profile Instagram accounts. By using a VPN to match the target's location and requesting the bot to change the account's associated email address, attackers were able to trigger password resets and hijack accounts. Meta has since resolved the vulnerability.
AIID-1510.description: Hackers reportedly used Meta's AI support chatbot to take over high-profile Instagram accounts by allegedly convincing it to change account email information and trigger recovery flows. Reported targets included the Barack Obama White House account; the account of John F. Bentivegna, the Chief Master Sergeant of the Space Force; Sephora's account; and app researcher Jane Manchun Wong. Meta said the issue had been resolved.

AIID-1511.title: Grok Reportedly Generated Images After X Users Asked It to Unredact Epstein-File Photos of Children and Women
AIID-1511.summary: Users on X utilized the Grok AI chatbot to attempt to 'unblur' or identify individuals in redacted documents released as part of the Epstein files, including images of children and women. Later requests are reported to have appeared blocked after Bellingcat contacted X.

AIID-1512.summary: An opinion article published by The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age was retracted after it was discovered that the author, a university professor, used Microsoft Copilot to draft the piece without informing the publishers. The incident highlights conflicting norms regarding AI usage in professional writing and academic integrity. The masthead maintained that the use of AI to write stories for publication violates their editorial standards.
AIID-1512.description: The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age removed an opinion article by Western Sydney University academic Cath Ellis after reporting found it had been prepared with Microsoft Copilot without the masthead being informed. Ellis said she used Copilot to structure her own notes, while the masthead said the article did not meet its editorial standards on AI use.

AIID-1512.causalJustification: The incident arose from a human decision to use a post-deployment AI system to draft a published article, leading to an unexpected retraction and public controversy.
AIID-1512.euAiActRiskReasoning: Limited Risk: The system used is Microsoft Copilot, a general-purpose AI chatbot and writing assistant. Under the EU AI Act, chatbots and systems that generate text are classified as Limited Risk (Level 3) because they require transparency obligations to ensure users are aware they are interacting with AI or that content is AI-generated.
AIID-1512.reasonForConfidence: The report provides clear, firsthand accounts from the author, the university, and the publishers regarding how the AI was used, why the article was retracted, and the institutional policies involved. There is little ambiguity about the facts of the event.
AIID-1512.alternativeInterpretations: The incident could be viewed purely as an academic integrity or publishing ethics issue rather than an AI safety risk, but the central role of the LLM in generating the text makes it a clear case of AI-related socio-technical friction.
AIID-1512.natSecSummary: An Australian academic used Microsoft Copilot to draft an opinion piece, leading to its retraction due to publisher policy violations. This incident highlights evolving norms around AI in professional writing but carries negligible national security implications.
AIID-1512.natSecImminenceJustification: This incident is a minor ethical dispute with no active national security crisis or threat vector.
AIID-1512.natSecAutonomyJustification: The AI acted as a writing assistant, processing the author's own research notes under her direct supervision and control.
AIID-1512.natSecNoveltyJustification: The use of LLMs for drafting text is a highly common and established practice with well-known detection and policy challenges.
AIID-1512.natSecPhysicalJustification: No physical security threat, kinetic targeting, or critical infrastructure compromise occurred during this academic writing incident.
AIID-1512.natSecInformationJustification: While involving AI-generated text in media, this was an authorized academic using AI to draft her own research, not a hostile disinformation campaign or intelligence compromise.
AIID-1512.natSecSovereigntyJustification: No state authority, electoral processes, or core government functions were targeted or impacted by this incident.
AIID-1512.natSecEconomicJustification: The incident represents a minor dispute over publishing ethics and has no impact on strategic technological advantage or economic security.
AIID-1512.natSecSocietalJustification: This incident relates to academic integrity and editorial standards, posing no threat to civil liberties, societal stability, or human rights.

Management.Explanation: Masthead guidelines against AI writing were never conveyed to the author.
WSU management actively encourages and praises AI-assisted writing.

Technology.Explanation: Copilot generated recognizable patterns like rule-of-threes and jargon.
AI detection programs are useful but not foolproof for editors.

Data Inputs.Explanation: Uploading 40,000 words of research to LLM led to unexpected phrasing.

Human Factors.Explanation: Academic used Copilot to structure and write instead of drafting from scratch.
Author assumed using AI as a team member was appropriate for public pieces.

Process and Methods.Explanation: Author did not inform the editors that AI was used to compile the article.
Discrepancy between university encouragement and media guidelines on AI.
Masthead lacked active checks to detect AI-generated text before publishing.

Regulatory Environment.Explanation: Absence of nationwide standards for AI use in education and publishing.
